brief.headline: Push for a 10–15% price cut to ₹0.65–0.80/pc on caps by qualifying Manjushree or Mold-Tek as a second source.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for ₹0.65–0.80/pc on 28 mm induction-wad PP caps (down from the ₹0.85–0.95/pc typical market band).
priceAsk.basis: The market ask band is ₹0.55–1.20/pc, with ₹0.85–0.95/pc typical. The verdict says there is modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume or looser spec — we spend ₹58.17 L a year, so volume justifies the lower end.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay in 15 days (cutting our wait from 30 days) in exchange for an extra 4–5% off the price.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster frees up ₹2.39 L of cash for us.

brief.financialLeverage: Suraj publishes no financials, so we don't know their health or how tight cash is for them. We spend ₹58.17 L a year — material enough to matter, but we have no visibility into their size or margins. Without their numbers, our leverage comes from the market: caps are widely available, and we have strong alternates lined up. The plan is to use competition and the threat of a second source to move price, not to squeeze on payment terms we can't see inside.

evidence.point: Market asking price for 28 mm PP caps, typical band
Market verdict on price headroom at volume
evidence.figure: modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80/pc at higher volume / looser spec

evidence.point: Cash freed if we pay 15 days faster

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter — pharma bottles, caps, preforms. Revenue ₹2569.83 Cr, health score B (65/100). Top second-source candidate; already qualified for packaging.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (pails, containers, pharma); strong, profitable. Revenue ₹1010.97 Cr, health score B (73/100). Robust alternate for bottles and closures; already qualified for packaging.

alternates.name: Reliance Industries Limited
alternates.why: A lead to qualify (verify before RFQ) — pan-India manufacturer with medium confidence; could be a resin or cap source if specs align.

risks: Suraj's financials aren't public, so we're flying blind on their stability — if they're fragile, a hard push could backfire.

We have no internal price benchmark (no best price we pay or gap data), so the ₹0.65–0.80 target rests entirely on the market ask verdict — confirm the spec and volume assumptions before you lock it in.
The market backups (Reliance, Srichakra, IVL Dhunseri, Dalmia, Ganesha, Chemco) are leads, not qualified — don't present them as approved sources until procurement vets them.

If Suraj pushes back hard on price, test willingness to improve payment terms or tighten delivery windows instead — but without their cash position visible, we can't gauge how much that's worth to them.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We're spending ₹58.17 L a year with you on caps, and we're seeing the market at ₹0.65–0.80 for our volume — let's talk about how we get there together while we qualify a second source for supply security.
